_comment: FIXTURE COMBAT SESSIONS for the world tick's M3 parity guard. NOT production
data and never read from production: every monster and item id below is
validated against src/data at load (loadCombatSessions in ../combat.js), so a
renamed drop or a retuned monster turns the guard red instead of silently
testing the engine against a foe with no drop table.
userId is a nil-ish UUID; slot is 0. Nothing here is ever sent anywhere.
activeSinceOffsetMs / recoveringUntilOffsetMs are RELATIVE offsets in ms from
the scenario's fromMs, resolved by atSpan — a JSON file with absolute epochs
THE SET IS CHOSEN BY WHAT IT CAN TELL APART, not by coverage. The M1 guard was
green while the tick ran with auto-eat OFF and the accrue path ran with it ON,
because its only auto-eat fixture is a maxed character at 99 HP fighting a
slime who never reaches the 50% threshold. A fixture that cannot distinguish
the two contracts is not coverage; it is a green tick over an untested seam.

sessions.name: away goblin grind — the drop table, and the progress-op volume
why: The ordinary unattended night, and the one that measured the progress
cliff: up to 10 progress ops per window, and its worst nine consecutive
windows file 73 against hr_apply's c_max_progress_ops of 64 — the
highest of any fixture here. Also the only fixture that
reaches the rare rows (goblin_seal, goblin_totem, bronze_sword), which is
what makes the stream-health arm mean anything on a drop-table channel.

sessions.name: away, auto-eat on, the bag empties mid-span
why: THE FOOD FIXTURE, and the one that can tell the two contracts apart.
Measured: 8 meals eaten, the last at window 23 of 60, then three falls
AFTER the bag is empty. It is the fixture that turns the missing auto-eat
keys red (-65.0% gold, -62.5% xp against the accrue contract), and the
one where `hadFood` — a window-OPEN snapshot — genuinely diverges under
decomposition on delta.deaths[].food_in_bag.
driftBandWhy: C6's band measures NOISE between two draws of one distribution. This
character's ten minutes are decided by whether they survive — one extra
fall is about two minutes of knockout — so a resampled stream moves the
total for a reason that has nothing to do with the tick. Measured 54.1%,
with the decomposed chain surviving where the one-call span did not.
Widening the shared band to cover it would make it vacuous for the four
fixtures where it is meaningful. The starvation half of C6 still runs
here, and C2 — all sixty windows byte-identical against an independently
constructed accrue caller — is the stronger claim and is unaffected.

sessions.name: away, seven falls deep — the recovery ladder's rung
why: A character already six deaths into the day, so recoveryFor() charges a
3,840,000 ms rung rather than the first-death novice grace. It is the
fixture that turns the missing deathsTodayBefore/deathsLifetimeBefore red,
and the direction is a MINT: less knockout time is more paying time.
Its knockouts also cross window boundaries repeatedly, which is what the
recovery-boundary arm needs.

sessions.name: away, opens Knocked Out — the clock crosses the span
why: `recovering_until` is an ABSOLUTE server instant and the window OPENS
inside it, so no death happens in the span and nobody stood the character
up. Early windows are pure recovery: zero ticks, zero value, and they MUST
still settle (accrual.js `nothingHappened` excepts summary.recoverMs > 0,
RECOVER-2) or the knockout is re-served every cadence — recovery exploit
R1 arriving through the tick.

sessions.name: away, bow user vs rat — a second tick interval
why: 2112 ms rather than 2400 ms, so the alignment and tiling arms are not
measured against a single interval. A cadence that divides one character's
tick and not another's is exactly the case RULE 1 exists for.

sessions.name: away, three falls and the hero pulls back — the pointer ends
why: THE RETREAT (Recovery rev. 3). A foodless character's third fall ends the
run: the engine charges the rung, stamps recovering_until, writes the
death row, and THEN proposes delta.activity = idle. Measured: 58 of the
next 60 windows then refuse `no_activity`. Gather's pointer only moves on
a level stop, so this is the case the combat loop has that gather does
not — the batch must CLOSE on the activity key rather than fold across
it, because a flush window spanning two pointers journals one row about
two runs. Without this fixture C5 never runs and is a claim nobody made.
driftBandWhy: The run ENDS partway through the span, so the decomposed chain and the
one-call span are not measuring the same number of minutes and a value
drift between them is not noise about the tick. C5 is this fixture's
claim; the starvation half of C6 still runs, and C2 — every window
byte-identical against an independently constructed accrue caller — is
the stronger statement and is unaffected.

sessions.name: away, the NINE combat inputs — every one of them prices this window
why: M1f F4: a production combat tick receives nine inputs the old tick never
passed, and NO fixture could see them. Measured on the six sessions above:
enchant {} on all six, combatStyle null on all six, hearthfindReady false on
all six, combatXpAccruedToMs 0 on all six, and deaths_* non-zero on only two.
Dropping any of those four from the input changed NOTHING, so the parity
guard was green whether or not the tick passed them — blind, not wrong.
This session is built so each one MOVES the settled window, which is the
only thing that makes C2's byte-identity an assertion about them:
· autoEatEnabled / autoEatPct — a goblin_warlord (125 hp, 30 atk) takes
this fighter under the 70% line repeatedly; measured 3 meals.
· autoEatFood — the bag holds cooked_trout AND cooked_shark and NOMINATES
the trout, which is not what an unnominated scan picks. Drop the name
and a different item is debited.
· deathsTodayBefore / deathsLifetimeBefore — the food runs out and the
hero falls once inside the span, so recoveryFor() prices a SEVENTH fall
and not a first. Six deaths today is the measurement from the milestone.
· combatXpAccruedToMs — two minutes into the span, so the first windows
are inside the live credit's watermark and pay no combat XP.
· enchant — poison, which is goblin_warlord's elementWeak.
· combatStyle — 'aggressive', which is NOT the sword family's default
('controlled'), so the damage and the trained skill both move.
· buffs — a live damage buff, absolute `until` so no span can expire it.
hearthfindReady is TRUE here and is the ONE of the nine this session cannot
move: the combat sources are elk_king / grim_reaper / dragon at 1-in-14,940
to 1-in-24,860 PER KILL, so ten minutes of kills draws one roughly once in
five hundred seeds. Pinning a lucky seed would buy an arm that goes red the
next time an unrelated change shifts the stream. C16c pins the gate from
accrual.js's own source instead, and says so rather than counting a vacuous
arm as coverage.
driftBandWhy: Same reason as the auto-eat session, and larger: this span is decided
by whether the hero survives once the bag empties, and one extra fall
is minutes of knockout. Measured +118.7% gold, with the decomposed
chain surviving where the one-call span did not — a number about the
resampled stream, not about the tick. C6's band measures NOISE between
two draws of one distribution; widening it to cover this would make it
vacuous for the four fixtures where it is meaningful, so this session
declares N/A and C2's per-window byte-identity carries the weight.

sessions.name: ATTENDED — a live claim the tick must refuse, not price
why: THE ATTENDED HALF OF THE BOTH-PATH RULE (CLAUDE.md §4). `attendedClaim` is
the shape `hr_attended_kills` projects: kills the server has ALREADY
accepted and clamped since accrued_to. The accrue path pays
min(claimed, attendedKillCap, 3 x sim) - sim on top of the simulation;
every term of that is priced against the SPAN, so a decomposed window
would pay it once per window. The tick therefore REFUSES it (throws) and
this fixture is that refusal's exit code — plus the proof that the same
character, settled as ONE accrue window, is priced with the top-up.
